pr_title: Normalize cluster config & simplify binding IConfiguration to TOptions
pr_body:
Fixes #4086.

Unsure if we should also add some sugar methods like `ConfigureClusterId(string)` and `ConfigureSiloName(string)`. `ClusterId` is much more important than `SiloName`.

We could also consider setting `ClusterId` to `"default"` if it's not otherwise set.
pr_comments:
>We could also consider setting ClusterId to "default" if it's not otherwise set.

I'm concerned this could lead to error prone usage with people deploying multiple services that will end up joining a single cluster. It seems to be it is better to be explicit with `ClusterId`, unless their a natural unique ID to automatically pick up like deployment ID in Azure Cloud Services.

I'm alright with being explicit - in that case we should consider having a `ConfigureClusterId(string)` method, since everyone will need it.

I'll close the other PR. What about this one, though?

issue_context.title: SiloBuilder extensions/options usability issues
issue_context.body:
Let's track here all change that we should do in SiloBuilder extensions methods and options before release.

- [x] `UseDevelopmentClustering` is not very user friendly; user should be able to just call `siloBuilder.UseDevelopmentClustering()`, not `siloBuilder.UseDevelopmentClustering(options => ....)`
- [x] `ConfigureEndpoints` extensions are in namespace `Orleans.Configuration` instead of `Orleans.Hosting`
- [ ] The method to configure the cluster on the client is called `ConfigureCluster` but is called `Configure` on the silo

review_comments:
why are we removing those sugar methods on ClusterOptions while you are concerning user will forget configuring clusterId? My mental picture is, sugar method increase discoverability -> user tends to configure clusterId more. 

Am I missing anything ?

The naming 'ConfigureCluster' is too general and as Sergey pointed out (IIRC), it's seems strange to have a method called ConfigureCluster on the client.
It's either `ConfigureCluster(x)` or `Configure<ClusterOptions>(x)`.

Ah I see. I wonder should we add ConfigureClusterId sugar method in this case? since configuring clusterId seems so important now. Or we agreed that throw validation exception when it is not set is good enough?
if throwing validation exception is enough, then I can merge this pr
We can merge this and consider a configuration method separately
